profile.reading:
EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure describes access to more than 4.0 billion dollars in institutional capital available for data center investment, and states more than 6.0 billion dollars in data center assets developed, acquired, or managed, drawing on more than 140 years of collective data center experience across its executive team. The companys own site states 6 campuses transacted, developed, or operating globally and existing land and data center capacity of more than 470 IT megawatts, though it did not state a headquarters address, founding year, or the specific Mesa, Arizona or Santa Clara County, California markets on the fetched page, which appeared to have some figures redacted in the source material reviewed.

The registry here tracks 2 EdgeCore facilities, in Mesa, Arizona and Santa Clara County, California, both well-known large-scale data center markets consistent with a major wholesale campus developer. This specific facility, recorded in this registry under an EdgeCore-branded name, was not individually named in any prior operator-level research; its operator field was blank in the source data and is set here to EdgeCore based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand.
profile.research_note: New facility-phase research: operator field set from blank to EdgeCore based on the facility own name. Grouped update covering EdgeCore (Mesa AZ) and EdgeCore Silicon Valley (Santa Clara County CA).

reading.body:
EdgeCore Silicon Valley in Santa Clara County, California, publishes 72 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space, operated by .

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 7200 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 1800 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

EdgeCore Silicon Valley holds 1 published certification: LEED (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

California has 22 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 10 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 356 MW. EdgeCore Silicon Valley contributes 72 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
